article.title: NFL EDGE Thursday Evening Brief
article.dek: Both cards flipped this evening, the Colts are down both starting cornerbacks for tonight, and Baker Mayfield is trending to play Sunday.

items.headline: Both cards flipped this evening
paragraphs: The app's cards changed this evening. Hit Rate is now the Detroit Lions moneyline at -260 on FanDuel for Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. Balanced is now the New York Jets +3 at -106 on DraftKings for Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET.

This morning the cards were the Jaguars moneyline at -260 and the Vikings +3 at +100. The Jaguars moneyline is still on the board at -255 on FanDuel, and the Vikings +3 is still +100 — but neither holds a card tonight.
The Value card is still empty. The app found no +EV price on the board, and it says so plainly instead of forcing one.
items.takeaway: New cards tonight: Hit Rate is Lions moneyline -260, Balanced is Jets +3 at -106. Value is still empty.

items.headline: Tonight: the Colts are down both starting tackles and both starting cornerbacks
paragraphs: Inactives are out for Thursday night, and the morning's watch item is settled: Sauce Gardner is OUT with a calf injury. He did not practice all week. Charvarius Ward is out too, so Indianapolis plays without both starting cornerbacks — and without both starting tackles, Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis.

The Colts' other inactives are tight end Will Mallory, defensive tackle Jerry Tillery, and third quarterback Riley Leonard. Tackle Charlie Heck, who was questionable, had the designation removed and will play.

Houston is short too: defensive end Danielle Hunter, wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., running back Woody Marks, and tight end Brevin Jordan are out, plus guard Wyatt Teller, who was questionable with a back injury. Running back David Montgomery is back after missing four games.
items.takeaway: The Colts play tonight without both starting tackles and both starting cornerbacks. The Texans are without Hunter and Harrison Jr., but David Montgomery is back.

items.headline: Baker Mayfield practiced Thursday — and the app caught up
paragraphs: Baker Mayfield practiced on Thursday and looked fine, and he is trending to play Sunday at Detroit. That is a sharp turn from Wednesday, when he sat out practice and was reported to be a long shot to play.
Head coach Todd Bowles said the team will decide on Friday. The app has already moved: it now lists Mayfield — not Jalon Daniels — as Tampa Bay's expected starter. The change landed this afternoon.

Geno Smith is the other quarterback to watch. He was limited again on Thursday, his second straight limited practice, and he still says starting Sunday at the Chargers is the plan. The app still lists him as the Jets' expected starter.
items.takeaway: Mayfield practiced Thursday and is trending to play; the app now lists him as Tampa Bay's starter. Geno Smith was limited again but still plans to play.

items.headline: Weather: nothing changed since this morning
paragraphs: Thursday night is under a roof in Houston: about 68 degrees, wind about 4 mph. Weather is a non-factor tonight.

Sunday's windiest spot is still Chicago: the Saints-Bears game is about 49 degrees with wind about 15 mph, gusting to 32. Buffalo is about 61 degrees with wind about 12 mph, gusting to 26. Sunday night in Mexico City is about 66 degrees with a 76% chance of rain and wind about 2 mph.
The forecast has not moved since Tuesday. Weather is a fact, not an edge. The app prices the games, not the forecast.
items.takeaway: Mild everywhere, Thursday under a roof. Chicago is still the windiest spot at 15 mph with gusts to 32.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: How to read the flipped cards
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the pick the app thinks is most likely to win. It forgoes value for win probability. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate — a likely winner is not the same thing as a good price.

Lions moneyline -260 at FanDuel. At -260, every $2.60 you risk wins $1. The app's model gives Detroit about a 76% chance; the market says about 71%. The app's play-through is -269. That is the price where it stops being a bet, and -260 still clears it.

It is also the app's biggest stake of the week at 1.25 units. Balanced is Jets +3 at -106 on DraftKings — close to even money, a good starting point if you are new to this. Value is empty because nothing on the board is +EV, and the app says so plainly instead of forcing one.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate is Lions moneyline -260: the most likely winner, not a value play. Balanced is Jets +3 at -106. Value is empty because nothing is +EV.

items.headline: The app still thinks the big spreads are too fat — and it still did not bet any of them
paragraphs: The model's margins against the DraftKings spreads: Chiefs by about 6.3 against a 16.5-point spread. Bills by about 3.4 against 16.5. Texans by about 0.8 against 12.5. Bears by about 0.2 against 11.5. Jaguars by about 5.7 against 6.0 — the closest of the bunch.
Two more gaps joined them tonight: the model has Detroit by only about 1.7 against a 6-point spread, and Pittsburgh by about 1.8 against a 4.5-point spread for the Eagles.

None of those underdogs cleared the bar for a card. A gap is the start of the work, not the bet. If your book has a better number than the app's, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and let the app run it back through the model and give you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Seven big spreads, seven big model gaps, zero cards. The gap alone is not the bet — Check your price.

items.headline: Tonight the tickets and the money disagree on the moneyline
paragraphs: DraftKings' own published figures for tonight's game, read this evening: 76% of the tickets are on the Texans moneyline at -750, but 61% of the money is on the Colts at +533. The crowd is on the favorite. The bigger bets are on the dog.

That is the opposite of the spread split earlier this week, when most tickets were on the Colts +12.5 and most money was on the Texans. Different market, different bettors, different story — which is why you read the split for the bet you are actually considering.

A split like this is worth watching. It is not a pick by itself. The spread still sits at Texans -12.5, Pinnacle is at -13, and the app has no card on this game — its model has Houston by only about 0.8 against that 12.5-point spread.
items.takeaway: Most tickets are on the Texans moneyline, most money is on the Colts. The crowd and the bigger money disagree — and that disagreement is worth watching, not following blindly.

items.headline: What to watch, and how to use it
paragraphs: Watch the Colts moneyline price. It already shortened from +550 on Thursday afternoon to +533 at DraftKings, and the Colts' share of the money ticked up from 58% to 61% across the evening. If it keeps shortening toward +450, the big money is still coming in. If it drifts back past +600, the moment has passed.
If you liked the Colts at +12.5, this split is a reason to wait for a better number — not a reason to chase the moneyline at +533. Sharper, price-sensitive bettors let the price come to them.
If you want to play it, run your price through Check first. Type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your number.
items.takeaway: Watch the Colts moneyline: shorter toward +450 means the big money is still coming; back past +600 means the moment passed. Wait for the price — don't chase it.

items.headline: Thursday's total jumped a point
paragraphs: The Colts-Texans total moved from 43.5 this morning to 44.5 at DraftKings and FanDuel tonight. The spread held: Texans -12.5 at both books, -13 at Pinnacle.
The app caught the move. Its board shows 44.5. If your book still has the total at 43.5 and Check says bet, take it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number tomorrow.
items.takeaway: Total up a point to 44.5, spread still Texans -12.5. The app caught the total move.

items.headline: Kansas City got expensive again, Cincinnati drifted, Detroit got cheaper
paragraphs: Chiefs -15.5 at DraftKings this morning, -16.5 tonight — back where they were on Wednesday morning. Pinnacle still shows -16. The model still has Kansas City by only about 6.3, so the move does not change anything on the card.

The Bengals spread drifted too: -6.5 at DraftKings this morning, -6.0 tonight, and their moneyline is still -270 at FanDuel. The Lions spread came down a point on the Mayfield news: -7.0 this morning, -6.0 at DraftKings tonight. The Jaguars moneyline also ticked down, from -260 to -255 at FanDuel.

One timing note: the Mayfield decision lands on Friday. If he is ruled out, Detroit likely gets more expensive — so if you like the Lions, the -6.0 is there now. If you like Tampa Bay, waiting for Friday could buy you a better number.
items.takeaway: Chiefs back to -16.5, Bengals down to -6.0, Lions down to -6.0 on the Mayfield news. Tampa Bay backers can wait for Friday; Detroit backers should take the -6.0 now.

items.headline: Friday brings the Mayfield decision — check back in the morning
paragraphs: Thursday night is underway, and the board's next refresh lands tomorrow morning. The Mayfield decision is the one to watch: if your book still prices Tampa Bay like Jalon Daniels is starting, run it through Check now — the app already lists Mayfield as the expected starter.
Settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself. Log the losers too — the record is only useful if it tells the truth.
items.takeaway: Check your Tampa Bay price against the app's Mayfield listing now, then check back tomorrow morning for the decision. And log the losers — the tracker only works if it's honest.
